_**Agent (auto-smart)**_

`plan.md` is a **backend-only** plan. Frontend is out of scope. RAG (D–F) is written but **blocked** until Phase C is marked complete **and** you confirm in chat.

There are **six lettered phases**, with B split into five slices:

| Phase | What it is | Status in the plan |
|--------|------------|--------------------|
| **A** | Application setup: Maven Wrapper, Boot config, Compose Postgres, Liquibase ticket tables, Testcontainers smoke. Empty HTTP surface; no ticket APIs yet. | not started |
| **B** | Ticket **CRUD** (no status transitions). | — |
| **B1** | Domain enums, constants, sort whitelist. | not started |
| **B2** | Persistence entities and repositories. | not started |
| **B3** | DTOs, mapping, validation, CRUD application service. | not started |
| **B4** | Controllers, query validation, error handling. | not started |
| **B5** | Persistence across restart. | not started |
| **C** | State machine and legal PATCH `status` (T1–T5; illegal pairs → 409). | not started; **RAG gate** |
| **D** | RAG ingestion, embeddings, PgVector schema. | blocked |
| **E** | Ingest wiring from ticket service (after-commit hooks). | blocked |
| **F** | AI ask API (`POST /api/ai/ask`, retrieve-then-generate). | blocked |

**Order:** A → B1–B5 → C → **stop for your confirmation** → D → E → F.

Phase C is the hard gate (**G7** + **G8**): no Spring AI, embeddings, vector table use, or `/api/ai/ask` until C is complete and you say to start RAG.

<think><details><summary>Thought Process</summary>
Spring Boot 3.5.16 is the latest general availability release.

Generating the Maven project via start.spring.io with Spring Boot 3.5.16.

The generated project includes web, JPA, validation, Liquibase, PostgreSQL, and Testcontainers dependencies. A manual pom.xml with Maven wrapper is a fallback if Spring Boot 3.5.16 is unavailable. Testcontainers integration for Spring Boot 3.5 is being configured.

Testcontainers dependencies are scoped to test. The PostgreSQL container uses the pgvector/pgvector:pg16 image. Liquibase will run before Hibernate validate. With no entities in Phase A, Hibernate validate will pass without errors.

Jackson will serialize dates as ISO-8601 UTC strings rather than timestamps. Hibernate ddl-auto is set to validate. The database timezone is UTC. Unknown properties will cause deserialization failures. Default property inclusion is left as-is.

A ConfigurationProperties record will hold API pagination defaults. The default page size is 20 and the maximum is 100. Relaxed YAML binding maps these values automatically. The PostgreSQL datasource URL will use a localhost fallback with environment variable support.

Local database credentials will default to "tickets" in both the YAML and Docker Compose files. Environment variables will override these defaults at runtime. The .env.example file will document the required variable names. Local defaults match the Compose configuration so the application starts immediately after docker compose up.

Docker Compose mounts a named volume for PostgreSQL data persistence. Liquibase will define a descending index on the ticket table's created_at column. GIN indexes require raw SQL changesets.

Liquibase will run three changelogs in sequence: 001 for the ticket tables, 002 for extensions, and 003 for indexes. The master changelog includes each file in order. A GIN trigram index on the title column will use pg_trgm. The pg_trgm extension will be created if missing. The ticket number sequence starts at 1001.

PostgreSQL UUID type is used for ticket identifiers. Liquibase is enabled by pointing to the master changelog on the classpath. A smoke test will use Testcontainers to spin up a PostgreSQL container and dynamically inject its JDBC URL into Spring Boot properties.

The Testcontainers smoke test will also inject the container's username and password dynamically. It will verify schema application by querying information_schema.tables for the ticket table and checking the ticket_number_seq sequence value. Spring-JDBC is already included through the data-jpa dependency.

The smoke test will also verify indexes on the ticket and ticket_comment tables. Backend target directories are already excluded by the global .gitignore. The .env file will be omitted from version control. A brief backend README will be added for local startup instructions. Graphify will be updated after code changes. The Maven wrapper will be generated from the Spring Initializer zip. Default Application.java from the generator will be excluded if the package name is incorrect. The repository root will be checked for a parent POM.
</details></think>

**Phase A is done.** The backend is a runnable Spring Boot app under `backend/` with a relational schema and a green smoke test. Ticket APIs are still out of scope until Phase B.

**What landed**
- Spring Boot **3.5.16** (latest Boot 3 GA), Java 21, Maven Wrapper
- Package `com.ticketmanagement`, CORS for `http://localhost:5173`, list defaults `20` / `100`
- Compose Postgres: `pgvector/pgvector:pg16` (local only; tests do not use it)
- Liquibase **001–003**: `ticket`, `ticket_comment`, `ticket_number_seq` from 1001, `pg_trgm`, agreed indexes
- No `ticket_vector_chunk`, no `rag/` types, no Spring AI

**Proof:** `cd backend && ./mvnw test` passed. The smoke test starts the context on Testcontainers, applies Liquibase, and checks tables, sequence start `1001`, and index names.

**Local run:** `docker compose up -d` in `backend/`, then set `SPRING_DATASOURCE_*` (names in `.env.example`) and `./mvnw spring-boot:run`.

Phase B (CRUD, still no status transitions) is next when you want it.
